exposure: universal transvaginal ultrasound cervical length (CL) screening
outcome: screening value of TVCL in predicting SPTB (spontaneous preterm birth)
cohort: Eligible women with singleton pregnancies who accepted and underwent second-trimester cervical length screening at one tertiary care facility between 2012-2015.
finding: Universal cervical length screening was successfully implemented with an 82.5% acceptance rate, high compliance with progesterone treatment (94.7%), and a higher rate of spontaneous preterm birth (35%) in women with a short cervix compared to those with a TVCL > 25 mm (6.3%).
